Directions hearing over deaths of Victoria police officers Neal Thompson and Vadim De Waart-Hottart told of new details of Porepunkah shooting Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The alleged sexual assault of a child has been revealed as the reason for a search warrant against Dezi Freeman that ended with him shooting dead two Victorian police officers. Fresh details into the August deaths of Det Leading Sen Const Neal Thompson, 59, and Sen Const Vadim De Waart-Hottart, 35, at Freeman’s home were detailed in a coroner’s court directions hearing on Monday morning. Freeman, who was also known as Desmond Filby, was shot dead by police in March, after being discovered at makeshift campsite about 150km away.

The counsel assisting the inquest, Linsday Spence, said in his opening summary police had executed the warrant after receiving disclosure of an alleged sexual assault involving a child under the age of 16, as well as an attempt to involve a child in the production of child abuse material. “The purpose of the search warrant was for the locating and seizure of electronic devices that were to be interrogated for the potential presence of child abuse material,” he told the court. “It was also intended that the person of interest was to be arrested and subsequently interviewed.” The two killed officers were among a team of police serving a warrant at his home at Porepunkah, 310km northwest of Melbourne. After Freeman killed them, he led police on one of the nation’s largest manhunts.

The seven-month search for the 56-year-old ended when he died in a hail of police bullets on a remote property in Thologolong, near Walwa on the Victoria-NSW border, on 30 March. State coroner Liberty Sanger was holding directions hearings for the inquest into the deaths of the police officers on Monday morning, before turning her attention to Freeman’s death in the afternoon. The dates and the scope of the inquests – and decisions on who would give evidence – were expected to be set on Monday. The coroner will examine the three deaths in detail to establish how they died and what could be done to prevent future deaths, according to Queensland University of Technology forensic criminologist Dr Claire Ferguson.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Directions hearing over deaths of Victoria police officers Neal Thompson and Vadim De Waart-Hottart told of new details of Porepunkah shooting

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The alleged sexual assault of a child has been revealed as the reason for a search warrant against Dezi Freeman that ended with him shooting dead two Victorian police officers.

Fresh details into the August deaths of Det Leading Sen Const Neal Thompson, 59, and Sen Const Vadim De Waart-Hottart, 35, at Freeman’s home were detailed in a coroner’s court directions hearing on Monday morning.

Freeman, who was also known as Desmond Filby, was shot dead by police in March, after being discovered at makeshift campsite about 150km away.

The counsel assisting the inquest, Linsday Spence, said in his opening summary police had executed the warrant after receiving disclosure of an alleged sexual assault involving a child under the age of 16, as well as an attempt to involve a child in the production of child abuse material.

“The purpose of the search warrant was for the locating and seizure of electronic devices that were to be interrogated for the potential presence of child abuse material,” he told the court.

“It was also intended that the person of interest was to be arrested and subsequently interviewed.”

The two killed officers were among a team of police serving a warrant at his home at Porepunkah, 310km northwest of Melbourne.

After Freeman killed them, he led police on one of the nation’s largest manhunts.

The seven-month search for the 56-year-old ended when he died in a hail of police bullets on a remote property in Thologolong, near Walwa on the Victoria-NSW border, on 30 March.

State coroner Liberty Sanger was holding directions hearings for the inquest into the deaths of the police officers on Monday morning, before turning her attention to Freeman’s death in the afternoon.

The dates and the scope of the inquests – and decisions on who would give evidence – were expected to be set on Monday.

The coroner will examine the three deaths in detail to establish how they died and what could be done to prevent future deaths, according to Queensland University of Technology forensic criminologist Dr Claire Ferguson.

“They’ll have a full reconstruction of what actually occurred, and that might be establishing people’s exact positioning in the scenes and forensic evidence,” Ferguson said.

Speculat

---

[Lähde: 7NEWS Australia]
The owner of the Porepunkah property where Dezi Freeman murdered two police officers has broken his silence about that fateful day.

Andrew Swift was outside Dezi’s den when the gunshots rang out and rushed to help the officers.

For the first time, he has offered an eyewitness account and a look inside the scene that was filmed in October of the crime that captivated a nation.

Know the news with the 7NEWS app: Download today

Two months after Dezi Freeman shot and killed two police officers in Porepunkah, Swift gave an interview.

It was released on YouTube on Saturday morning and includes a tour of the caravan with bullet holes.

Andrew says he was in his office when Dezi’s wife Mali called him on the morning of the shooting.

“She said, ‘Andy, come down to the bus, the police are here and they’re surrounded the bus and they’re trying to get in’,” he said.

He says he tried to reason with Dezi and when shots rang out, he thought they came from police.

“And then we don’t really know too much about what occurred in here,” he said from inside caravan.

Swift was overcome with emotion when he recalled how he came to the aid of the third officer, who was shot, but survived.

“He was wearing dark coloured pants but you could tell they were all wet from blood, from a gunshot somewhere down on his lower half,” he said.

Swift said he rushed the policeman to an awaiting ambulance.

After the incident, he was then stopped from entering his property for two weeks.

“Effects of that morning still resonate strongly with us,” he said.

Victoria Police declined to comment on the video as the case is currently before the coroner.

payload.title: Kuolintutkinta: Porepunkahin ampumisen taustalla oli lapsen seksuaalirikosepäilyä koskenut etsintälupa
payload.summary: Australiassa kuolintutkinnan valmisteluistunnossa on kuultu uusia tietoja Porepunkahin ampumisesta, jossa kaksi Victorian osavaltion poliisia kuoli. Poliisi oli mennyt Dezi Freemanin kotiin lapsen seksuaalirikosepäilyä koskeneen etsintäluvan vuoksi.
payload.content:
Australiassa Victorian osavaltion kuolintutkinnan valmisteluistunnossa on kerrottu, että Dezi Freemaniin kohdistunut etsintälupa liittyi epäiltyyn alle 16-vuotiaaseen lapseen kohdistuneeseen seksuaalirikokseen ja yritykseen saada lapsi mukaan lapsiin kohdistuvaa hyväksikäyttömateriaalia sisältävän aineiston tuottamiseen. Etsintäluvan täytäntöönpano Freemanin kodissa Porepunkahissa päättyi kahden poliisin kuolemaan.

## Poliisit olivat suorittamassa etsintälupaa

Istunnossa käsiteltiin etsivä ylikonstaapeli Neal Thompsonin, 59, ja vanhemman konstaapeli Vadim De Waart-Hottartin, 35, kuolemia. He kuuluivat poliisiryhmään, joka oli mennyt Freemanin kotiin Porepunkahiin, noin 310 kilometriä Melbournesta luoteeseen.

Kuolintutkintaa avustava juristi Linsday Spence kertoi avausyhteenvedossaan, että etsintäluvan tarkoituksena oli löytää ja takavarikoida elektronisia laitteita. Laitteita oli määrä tutkia sen selvittämiseksi, oliko niissä lapsiin kohdistuvaa hyväksikäyttömateriaalia. Spencen mukaan tarkoituksena oli myös ottaa epäilty kiinni ja kuulustella häntä.

Freeman, joka tunnettiin myös nimellä Desmond Filby, ampui kaksi poliisia etsintäluvan täytäntöönpanon yhteydessä. Tapaus käynnisti yhden Australian suurimmista ajojahdeista.

## Seitsemän kuukauden etsintä päättyi maaliskuussa

Freemania etsittiin seitsemän kuukauden ajan. Etsintä päättyi 30. maaliskuuta, kun 56-vuotias Freeman kuoli poliisin luoteihin syrjäisellä kiinteistöllä Thologolongissa, Walwan lähellä Victorian ja Uuden Etelä-Walesin rajalla. Hänet oli löydetty väliaikaiselta leiripaikalta noin 150 kilometrin päässä.

## Kuolintutkinta kattaa kolme kuolemaa

Osavaltion kuolinsyyntutkija Liberty Sanger käsitteli maanantaina aamupäivällä poliisien kuolemia koskevaa tutkintaa. Iltapäivällä huomion oli määrä siirtyä Freemanin kuolemaan. Istunnossa odotettiin päätöksiä tutkintojen aikataulusta, laajuudesta ja siitä, ketkä kutsutaan todistamaan.

Kuolintutkinnan tarkoituksena on selvittää kolmen kuoleman olosuhteet ja arvioida, mitä vastaavien kuolemien ehkäisemiseksi voitaisiin tehdä tulevaisuudessa. Queensland University of Technologyn oikeuskriminologi Claire Fergusonin mukaan tutkinnassa tarkastellaan kuolemia yksityiskohtaisesti juuri näiden kysymysten selvittämiseksi.
summary_bullets: Victorian kuolintutkinnan valmisteluistunnossa kuultiin uusia tietoja Porepunkahin ampumisesta.
Etsintälupa liittyi epäiltyyn alle 16-vuotiaaseen lapseen kohdistuneeseen seksuaalirikokseen ja hyväksikäyttömateriaaliepäilyyn.
Neal Thompson ja Vadim De Waart-Hottart kuolivat etsintäluvan täytäntöönpanon yhteydessä.
Dezi Freeman kuoli myöhemmin poliisin luoteihin seitsemän kuukauden etsinnän jälkeen.
